FundEditor.Title: Fund
FundEditor.Rebalance: Rebalance back to its starting mix
FundEditor.DistributionHint: An accumulating fund adds its holdings' dividends to its unit value. A distributing one sets them aside and pays holders cash each month or quarter (or reinvests it for those who switch reinvestment on). A redemption delay holds sellers' money for that many days after they sell.
FundEditor.RebalanceHint: Rebalancing resets the holdings to the mix the fund had when it was created or last edited, so winners do not take over. The manager's edge adds (or, if negative, subtracts) that much a year on top of what the holdings earn. Use it for an actively managed fund.
FundEditor.ComponentsHint: One company per line: ticker and weight, for example ARA 30. Weights are shared out in proportion.

Up.1: I'm hearing good things behind the scenes at {name} ({ticker}). Something has gone their way, and it may not be in the price yet.

Down.8: There's a long face going round the {ticker} crowd. I can't tell you why, only that it's a bad one.

Hedge.1: Rumours only, and I never said it. It can take a few days to show, if it shows at all.
Hedge.2: Take it with a pinch of salt. These things are right more often than they should be, and wrong just often enough to hurt.
Hedge.3: I can't prove any of it. Do what you like with it.
Hedge.4: It might be nothing. It might take a week to matter. Watch the price.
Hedge.5: You didn't hear this from me.
Hedge.6: Nothing is certain until it's in the price, and by then it's too late to care.

WarningLine.1: Some of your recent trades have lined up very neatly with news that came out afterwards. I am not accusing anyone, but people in my line of work notice that sort of thing.
WarningLine.2: I have been hearing questions about the timing of certain trades, and some of them are yours.
WarningLine.3: Your account has been looked at. Nothing official, but looked at, and I would rather you heard it from me.
WarningLine.4: There is talk about how well your trades have been timed around corporate news. Talk like that has a way of becoming more than talk.

WarningAdvice.1: If I were you I would trade less around company news for a while.
WarningAdvice.2: Keep your head down for a bit and let it blow over.
WarningAdvice.3: I would think hard before you do that again.

EnquirySubject.2: NCPD Financial Crimes: a few questions

EnquiryLine.1: NCPD Financial Crimes is carrying out a routine review of trading activity around a number of recent corporate announcements. Your account has come up. No action is being taken at this time.
EnquiryLine.2: This is a courtesy notice. Trades on your account have been flagged for review as part of an ordinary enquiry into the timing of trades around company news.
EnquiryLine.3: Your recent trading has been selected for a routine compliance review. You are not required to respond, and no finding has been made.

EnquiryAdvice.1: We would remind you that trading on information not available to the public is an offence.
EnquiryAdvice.2: Further activity of this kind may result in a formal investigation.

Fine.Subject: Notice of penalty
Fine.Line1: Following a review of your trading around recent corporate announcements, a penalty of {amount} eb has been taken from your brokerage balance.
Fine.Short: Your balance did not cover it. {amount} eb remains unpaid and has been noted against your name.
Fine.Line2: This notice is final. Further activity of this kind will be referred for prosecution.

Freeze.Subject: Account restriction
Freeze.Line1: Your brokerage account has been frozen for {days} while we complete a review of your trading. You cannot place orders or withdraw funds in that time. Open orders have been voided.
Freeze.Line2: You may still pay money in. The restriction will lift on its own.

Dropped.Subject: Our arrangement
Dropped.Line1: Your broker can no longer act for you. Any orders still open through them have been cancelled.
Dropped.Line2: You are free to choose another broker, though this one will not take you back for some time.

GMConsole.Title: Market GM Console
GMConsole.CalendarAhead: Hand advances have taken the market {days} day(s) past the calendar ({calendar}). Dividends, fund distributions, IPOs and statements fall due on the market date.
GMConsole.CalendarManual: In manual mode the market date moves only when you advance the market; the calendar shows {calendar}. Dividends, fund distributions, IPOs and statements fall due on the market date.
GMConsole.AdvanceDayHint: Move game time on by one whole day in a single step, and the calendar with it. Delays, sentiment changes and heat windows count it as a day. In the in-world clock mode a tick is only a few minutes of one.
GMConsole.AlignCalendarConfirm: Move Simple Calendar forward {days} day(s), to the market date? In-world time passes for everything that reads the calendar. The market itself does not move.
GMConsole.InvalidDays: Enter a whole number of ticks, 1 or more.
GMConsole.ResetConfirm: This erases all prices and history and starts every company again from its initial price. Player portfolios are not affected. Continue?
GMConsole.DeleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its journal is removed and the company leaves the market.
GMConsole.ActionFailed: That did not work. Check the values and that you are the active GM.
GMConsole.FundsHint: Funds pool several companies into one tradable unit. Their value follows the companies' prices. Players can only trade them through a broker.
GMConsole.CloseFundConfirm: Close {name}? Every holder is paid the current value in cash and the fund is removed.
GMConsole.DirectTermsHint: Direct trades fill at once and cost {commission} plus {flatFee} eb, from a CorpNet terminal after an Accounting check at DV {dv} (network: {network}). Brokers are always slower and cheaper. Change these in module settings.
GMConsole.BrokersHint: A broker's speed and fees come from their Accounting skill (INT plus level) on their character sheet. A contact with no sheet uses the rating set here.
GMConsole.RemoveBrokerHint: Remove this broker from the market. Their character and Night City Messenger contact are not changed. Only possible when no character is using them.
GMConsole.RemoveBrokerConfirm: Remove {name} as a broker? Their character and Night City Messenger contact stay exactly as they are, and you can make them a broker again later.

RemoveBrokerRefused.assigned: Cannot remove this broker while characters use them: {names}. They must choose another broker first.
RemoveBrokerRefused.busy: Cannot remove this broker yet: {names} still have orders or a withdrawal with them. Wait for those to finish.
RemoveBrokerRefused.unknown: That broker is no longer there.
RemoveBrokerRefused.gm-only: Only a GM can do that.

GMConsole.NoBrokers: No brokers yet. Make a character or contact a broker to let players hire them.
GMConsole.TerminalGrantsHint: Characters on a CorpNet-connected device can open a trading session. Grant access here for a terminal that is not on the network.
GMConsole.UndoHint: Step the market back one tick. Not possible once a player's money has moved because of that tick, or after a split, price change or new company.
GMConsole.UndoDone: The market is back at tick {tick}. Advancing again re-runs the tick, with the same random numbers unless you change the controls first.

Undo.not-active-gm: Only the active GM can undo a tick.
Undo.nothing-to-undo: There is no tick to undo.
Undo.settled: Players' money has already moved because of that tick (a fill, a dividend or a paid withdrawal), so it cannot be undone.

Controls.SentimentHint: A bias nudges prices up or down each day for a while, in units of each stock's normal daily swing. Strength is -3 to 3. Try 0.5 for a gentle push.
Controls.ShockHint: A one-off shock. The price eases toward the new level after the delay, then partly settles back. Use the percentage the price should move by.
Controls.Headline: Public headline (optional)
Controls.HeadlineHint: Shown to players in the News tab
Controls.SetPriceHint: A blunt tool: the price changes at once and is logged. Moving fair value too stops the market pulling the price straight back.

Actions.SpecialDividendHint: Pays every holder now, once. Shares bought today do not qualify.
Actions.SplitHint: An N-for-1 split: holders get N times the shares, the price divides by N, and cost per share adjusts. Charts stay continuous.
Actions.SplitConfirm: Split {name} {ratio}-for-1? Every holder's shares and open orders are adjusted.
Actions.BuyoutHint: The company is acquired. Holders are paid in cash at this price and the stock is retired.
Actions.BuyoutConfirm: Buy out {name} at {price} eb per share? Holders are paid and open orders are cancelled.
Actions.EndHint: Delisting pays holders the last price. Bankruptcy pays nothing and records the loss.
Actions.DelistConfirm: Delist {name}? Holders are paid its last price in cash.
Actions.BankruptConfirm: Declare {name} bankrupt? Every holder loses their position with no payout.

Gig.Title: Gig outcomes
Gig.Intro: When a gig is completed or failed in Night City Map, the bridge sends the result here. The client is matched to a company and its share price reacts after a short delay: a success helps a little, a failure hurts more, and a bigger reward moves it further.
Gig.BridgeMissing: The Night City Map bridge module is not active, so gigs will not arrive by themselves. You can still report an outcome by hand below.
Gig.ApprovalOn: Impacts wait for your approval. Change this in module settings.
Gig.ApprovalOff: Impacts are applied automatically once the client is matched.
Gig.NeedsMappingHint: These clients could not be matched to a company. Pick one, or ignore the client. The choice is remembered for later gigs from the same client.
Gig.ReviewHint: Change the size, the delay or the headline if you like, then approve. The headline is published when the price starts to move.
Gig.MappingsHint: A saved mapping always wins over name matching. You can also tag a gig's notes with [NCI: ARA] to name its company, or [NCI: ignore] to skip it.
Gig.ReportHint: For gigs that were not run through the map. Leave the company blank to find it from the client name.

Heat.Title: Insider-trading heat
Heat.Intro: A gig outcome is private until its price effect starts to show. A character who buys the client before good news, or sells before bad news, in that gap draws heat. Heat is hidden from players, runs from 0 to 100, and halves about every week.
Heat.Off: Heat tracking is switched off in module settings, so nothing is being recorded.
Heat.PhaseNote: Players are warned as heat builds: a nervous word from their broker, then a routine enquiry from NCPD Financial Crimes. At the top a penalty is chosen: a fine, a frozen account, or a broker who walks away. Anything that costs a player something waits here for you, unless you turn approval off in settings.
Heat.SetHeatHint: Set this character's heat directly. Zero clears it.
Heat.ExposureHint: Each open business's hidden Exposure, which raids and regulators' cases draw on. Set it by hand for what happened at the table; players only ever see its band.
Heat.ExposureSet: Set this business's Exposure directly. Zero clears it.
Heat.PenaltiesHint: What an investigation found. Change the amount or length if you like, then approve; dismiss to let it go. Approving carries it out at once and tells the player.
Heat.BanDays: Days it will not take them back

Penalty.dropBroker: Their broker walks away, and will not take them back for {days} days

Result.not-gm: Only the active GM can do that.

Notice.Pending: An investigation into {name} has found something. It is waiting for your approval in the Heat tab.

Heat.WindowsHint: Open from the moment a gig outcome is reported until its effect shows on the price. Trades placed inside are checked once it closes and any orders placed in it have filled.
Heat.AwaitingFills: closed, waiting for orders to fill

TierHint.noticed: 25-49. Their broker sends a nervous warning.
TierHint.flagged: 50-74. NCPD sends an enquiry, and broker orders are a day slower and cost half as much again.
TierHint.investigated: 75 and up. A penalty is chosen: a fine, a frozen account, or a broker who walks away.

Panel.Title: Cover your tracks
Panel.Intro: People have noticed how you trade. You can try to make it go away, but each try takes a skill roll and costs money whether it works or not, and cannot be repeated for a while. A bribe that is refused makes things worse.
Panel.Frozen: Your account is frozen until day {until}. You cannot trade or withdraw until then, but you can still pay money in.
Panel.BrokerBan: Your old broker will not take you back until day {until}.

Result.critical: {action}: a perfect job. The trail goes cold. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.success: {action}: it works. Things should quiet down. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.failure: {action}: it does not take. Nothing changes. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.fumble: {action}: it goes badly, and people will have noticed. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)

quash.Name: Call in a favour
quash.Desc: Backup, and a friend on the force. Takes a lot off your heat and stops any penalty waiting for you. It costs the same whatever comes of it, you can do it once a month, and a fumble makes things worse.

Result.success: Your friend makes it go away. Your heat is down, and any pending penalty is dropped.
Result.failure: Your friend can't help this time.
Result.fumble: The favour goes wrong, and more people are looking at you now.

mask.Name: Mask the pattern
mask.Desc: Run offsetting trades so the pattern is harder to read. Cheap, and you can do it often, but it only takes a little off.

books.Name: Cook the books
books.Desc: Make the paperwork tell a different story. A solid reduction for a modest price.

front.Name: Front company
front.Desc: Route your trades through a front. Takes a little off now, and halves the heat from any new audit for a week.

bribe.Name: Pay someone off
bribe.Desc: Put eddies in the right pocket. Takes the most off, but it is dear, hard to pull off, and a refusal gets talked about.

Tools.Title: Tools
Tools.Schema: Stored data is on schema v{version}.
Tools.CheckHint: Looks over companies, funds, the market, portfolios and the Night City Messenger link for anything broken or odd. Nothing is changed.
Tools.MacrosHint: Creates macros for opening the terminal and console, advancing the market a day and running the self-check. Foundry only lets Trusted players and above run script macros, so players can also use the button in the scene controls. Macros that already exist are left alone.
Tools.SuggestHint: Organisations named on Night City Messenger contacts and on gigs that are not companies on this market yet. Create one to open the company editor with the name filled in, or ignore it (gigs for an ignored client move no price).
Tools.TradeLogHint: The latest fills across every portfolio. Each portfolio only keeps its last 40 closed orders, so older ones drop off.

Verify.SummaryWarn: Self-check found {warn} warning(s). See the Audit tab or the console.
Verify.SummaryFail: Self-check found {fail} problem(s) and {warn} warning(s). See the Audit tab or the console.

Clock.RolledBack: The calendar went back, so the market went back with it, to tick {tick}. Ticking resumes as the date moves forward again.
Clock.RolledBackAhead: The calendar went back. The market rolled back {n} tick(s) but could go no further, so it is still {ahead} day(s) ahead of the calendar and will wait for the date to catch up.
Clock.Ahead: The calendar went back, but the market could not be rolled back (the ticks were too old, or players' money has moved). It is {ahead} day(s) ahead and will wait for the date to catch up.

Migration.Failed: Night City Investments could not update its stored data to schema v{version}. See the console. Nothing has been lost.

Keybindings.OpenTerminalHint: Not bound by default. Choose a key to open the market from anywhere.
Keybindings.OpenConsoleHint: GM only. Not bound by default.
Keybindings.OpenBusinessHint: Not bound by default. Opens the window where players run their businesses.

Voice.Label: Voice
Voice.Hint: Brokers with a character sheet write in the voice of the Personality on it. Others use the standard wording.

Log.glide: {company} glide scripted from {from} to {to} over {days} days
Log.gig: Gig outcome on {company}: {percent}%, showing in {days} day(s)
Log.undo: Undid tick {from}; the market is back at tick {to}

Preview.Title: Preview: {title} ({days} days ahead)
Preview.SummarySingle: Typical result (median): {median}, against {base} without it. Nine times in ten it lands between {low} and {high}. In {higher}% of {paths} simulated futures it ends higher than it would have without the change.
Preview.SummaryGroup: The average of the companies affected: {median} (median), against {base} without it. Nine times in ten between {low} and {high}. Higher than without the change in {higher}% of {paths} futures.
Preview.Note: The shaded bands are the middle 80% of simulated futures. They use their own random numbers, so this shows what is likely, not what will happen.

Reason.not-active-gm: Only the active GM can run a preview.
Reason.no-market: The market has not started yet.
Reason.no-targets: That target has no companies in it.
Reason.glide-too-steep: That glide asks for too big a move per day. Give it more days or a closer target.

Glide.Title: Scripted glide
Glide.Hint: Steer one company toward a target price over a number of days, landing on it exactly on the last day. Noise is how much of the usual day-to-day movement is kept on the way. Fair value follows, so the price does not snap back afterwards.
Glide.Started: Glide scheduled. It starts on the next tick.

Ipo.Title: Upcoming IPOs
Ipo.SubscribeHint: Shares are offered at {price} eb each. Your money is held, not spent, until the company lists. If the offer is oversubscribed you may receive fewer shares.
Ipo.OfferingHint: New shares are offered at {price} eb each. Your money is held, not spent, until the offering closes. If it is oversubscribed you may receive fewer shares.
Ipo.ListNowConfirm: List {name} on the market now and fill every subscription?
Ipo.EditorHint: To launch a company later, untick Listed above and set a date. It lists on that in-world date. Leave the date empty for no IPO.

SettlementDays.Name: Sale settlement delay (days)
SettlementDays.Hint: How long the proceeds of a sale take to become spendable. 0 is at once. While settling they count towards a portfolio's value but cannot be spent or withdrawn.

ShowTicker.Name: Show the market ticker strip
ShowTicker.Hint: A small strip at the top of the screen with the NC index and either the companies you have starred (up to four) or, if you have none, the day's biggest movers. Click it to open the Market Terminal. This setting is only for you.

TickMode.Name: Market tick mode
TickMode.Hint: How the market advances. In-world clock: one tick every set number of minutes of Simple Calendar time (below). If the calendar jumps forward the market catches up a game day at a time; if it goes back, the market just takes the new date. In-world day: one tick per day the calendar moves forward, and the market rolls back if the date is rolled back. Manual: only when the GM advances it.

RealTimeMinutes.Name: Tick interval (in-world minutes)
RealTimeMinutes.Hint: Only used when the tick mode is the in-world clock. One tick for every this many minutes of Simple Calendar time (24 hours of 60 minutes), however fast the clock runs. Anything that lasts days (a gig's delay, a sentiment change, a heat window, a broker's speed) is counted in game days, so this only sets how finely prices move.

GigImpactApproval.Name: GM approves gig impacts
GigImpactApproval.Hint: When on, market impacts from Night City Map gig outcomes wait for GM approval in the Gigs tab. When off they are applied automatically (a client that needs mapping, or only a close match, still waits).

GigImpacts.Name: Gig outcomes move the market
GigImpacts.Hint: Needs the Night City Map bridge module. When off, completed and failed gigs are ignored.

GigImpactScale.Name: Gig impact strength
GigImpactScale.Hint: Scales every gig impact. 1 is normal: a 1,000 eb job moves its client by about 1.5%, and a failure by more.

HeatEnabled.Name: Track insider-trading heat
HeatEnabled.Hint: Watch for trades on a gig's client in the gap before its effect shows on the price, and record a hidden heat score for each character (see the Heat tab). What the heat does to players is set by the next two settings.

HeatConsequences.Name: Warn and penalise suspicious trading
HeatConsequences.Hint: When on, rising heat has consequences: a warning from the player's broker, an enquiry from NCPD, slower and dearer broker orders while flagged, and at the top a penalty. It also lets warned players try to cover their tracks. When off, heat is only recorded.

HeatPenaltyApproval.Name: GM approves penalties
HeatPenaltyApproval.Hint: When on (the default), a fine, account freeze or dropped broker waits in the Heat tab for you to approve, change or dismiss. When off, penalties are carried out as soon as they are found. Warnings and enquiries are always sent.

HeatStrength.Name: Heat strength
HeatStrength.Hint: Scales how much heat each suspicious trade adds. 1 is normal: a medium trade (about 3,000 eb) is worth around 14 heat, two or three of them reach the first warning bracket, and larger trades draw more.

GigTips.Name: Mail rumours before a gig shows in the price
GigTips.Hint: Players who hold or watch the client and have turned on "Rumours" get a vague mail from their broker before the effect lands.

BrokerOrderMode.Name: Broker order handling
BrokerOrderMode.Hint: Auto: orders mailed to a broker are processed automatically after the broker's delay. Manual: each order waits in the GM queue.

DepositFee.Name: Deposit fee (eb)
DepositFee.Hint: Flat fee charged when a player deposits funds into their brokerage balance.

DirectExecution.Name: Direct order execution
DirectExecution.Hint: Only used when direct trading access is Open: when a player trades directly, fill at the next market tick or immediately at the current quote.

DirectCommission.Name: Direct trading commission (basis points)
DirectCommission.Hint: Commission on direct terminal trades, the most expensive way to trade. 100 basis points is 1%. Broker fees are always a share of this, set by the broker's Accounting skill.

DirectMode.Name: Direct trading access
DirectMode.Hint: Terminal: direct trades need a CorpNet terminal and a passed Accounting check. Open: anyone can trade directly with no check (the older behaviour).

DirectFlatFee.Name: Direct trading flat fee (eb)
DirectFlatFee.Hint: Charged on every direct trade. Brokers charge a lower share of this.

CorpnetDV.Name: Terminal check DV
CorpnetDV.Hint: The Accounting check a character must beat (INT + Accounting + 1d10) to open a direct trading session.

CorpnetNetwork.Name: Terminal network
CorpnetNetwork.Hint: The Night City Messenger network a device must be connected to for direct trading. Use the network's id, for example CORPNET.

SessionTicks.Name: Session length (market days)
SessionTicks.Hint: How many market days a passed check keeps direct trading open.

LockoutTicks.Name: Lockout after a failed check (market days)
LockoutTicks.Hint: How long a character is locked out after failing the check. A fumble doubles it.

DebugMode.Name: Debug logging
DebugMode.Hint: Write extra diagnostics to the browser console.

BusinessesEnabled.Name: Player businesses
BusinessesEnabled.Hint: Let players found and run their own businesses, with the Business window. Turning this off stops their weeks closing and refuses new requests; nothing is deleted.

CrewDowntime.Name: Business days come from Crew Tools downtime
CrewDowntime.Hint: On: extra time, project days and mentoring spend a character's Crew Tools downtime, and there is no weekly allowance, so business work competes with their other downtime. Remember to award days, and to open Downtime once for each character. Off: 3 business days a week for each voting partner.

ShareContacts.Name: Share contacts with players
ShareContacts.Hint: A character who picks a broker, or who founds a business with an NPC partner, gets that person in their Night City Messenger contacts.

PressFrequency.Name: Stories in the press
PressFrequency.Hint: How often corporations with a grudge run stories against player businesses. Off keeps the older smear events instead.

JobAuto.Name: Hire good job applicants automatically
JobAuto.Hint: Off: every passed application to an NPC's company waits on Pending. On: a solid roll or better is hired at once, and a narrow pass still waits for you.

PressApproval.Name: Press stories need GM approval
PressApproval.Hint: Each story waits on the GM Console's Pending tab until the GM lets it run or spikes it. The owners see nothing until then.

RoomEvents.Name: Back room events
RoomEvents.Hint: How often a back room that was worked last week draws trouble of its own.

DateFormat.Name: Date format
DateFormat.Hint: How dates show in this module's windows and mails, for everyone. Mails already sent keep the format they had.

Theme.Name: Colour theme
Theme.Hint: Your own choice, for this module's windows and ticker. Matching uses whichever skin and colours you have set in Pneuma's Visual Tools, and stays red if you have none active.

Underworld.Name: Underworld content
Underworld.Hint: Lets a business open an illegal back room, and make illegal items. A back room already open keeps running if you turn this off, but illegal lines stop; goods already made can still be fenced.

CampaignApproval.Name: Smears, leaks and stories need GM approval
CampaignApproval.Hint: A business's successful campaign against a company, or a Media's believed story, waits on the GM Console's Pending tab until the GM lets it run.

BusinessApproval.Name: New businesses need GM approval
BusinessApproval.Hint: A business that has passed its setup roll and has its money waits in the GM Console's Businesses tab until the GM lets it open.

SyndicatesEnabled.Name: Player syndicates
SyndicatesEnabled.Hint: Let players pool money in a syndicate that trades on the market as one account. Turning this off refuses new syndicate requests; existing syndicates keep their holdings and nothing is deleted.

ListingThreshold.Name: Listing threshold (eb)
ListingThreshold.Hint: The market valuation a chartered player company must reach, on three monthly reports in a row, before it can apply to list on the market. Lower it to let companies list sooner.

StaffMail.Name: Payslips by Messenger
StaffMail.Hint: Send a player character who works for a player business a Night City Messenger payslip from the market wire each week, with their wage attached to claim and anything still owed. Off (or with no Messenger), wages go straight to their sheet.

SyndicateMail.Name: Mail syndicate members
SyndicateMail.Hint: Send members a Night City Messenger mail from the market wire when a proposal opens and when it passes, fails or lapses, when an agreed payment fails, when their redemption is paid, and when the syndicate is wound up.

SyndicateApproval.Name: New syndicates need GM approval
SyndicateApproval.Hint: A syndicate a player founds waits in the GM Console's Syndicates tab until the GM approves it. Until then no money can be paid in.

BusinessWeekday.Name: Business week ends on
BusinessWeekday.Hint: Every business's operating week closes on the first market tick on or after this day. The day of your weekly session works well.

BusinessGrowthRate.Name: Business growth rate
BusinessGrowthRate.Hint: Scales how fast businesses build Reputation and Capacity. 1 is the calibrated pace; 1.5 suits a campaign that wants players' businesses to grow sooner.

Proposed.Subject: New proposal to vote on
Proposed.Body: Proposed by {name}. Vote in the market terminal's Portfolio tab, with the syndicate picked, before {date}.

Passed.Subject: Proposal passed
Passed.Body: Members holding more than half the units agreed.

Failed.Subject: Proposal turned down
Failed.Body: Members holding half the units or more said no.

Lapsed.Subject: Proposal lapsed
Lapsed.Body: Not enough members agreed before the vote closed.

Void.Subject: Proposal passed but could not be carried out

AgreedFailed.Subject: An agreed payment or trade failed
AgreedFailed.Body: The members agreed it, but it could not be done: {reason}.

Redeemed.Subject: Redemption paid
Redeemed.Body: {units} units of {name} were redeemed for {amount} eb, paid into your brokerage balance.

Dissolved.Subject: Syndicate wound up
Dissolved.Body: The syndicate has been dissolved. Its cash was paid into the members' brokerage balances by units.

Company.ReportWeek: Week {n} of {of} toward this month's report.
Company.ReportHint: Every four weeks the company sums its weeks in a report. In the last week an officer may prepare it with Accounting (Business at DV +2): a good roll reports a little more profit, a bad one less. Choosing Bold is aggressive reporting: twice the shift, and a trail that an audit may find later.
Company.NoReports: The first report comes four weeks after the charter.
Company.NotOfficer: You are a shareholder but not an officer: only officers take the company's actions, answer events and prepare its report. You can still help with a complementary check.
Company.OfficersHint: Officers run the company: they take its actions each week. Shareholders elect and dismiss them by a majority of the shares; a company always keeps at least one.
Company.AuditHint: An internal audit (Accounting, Business at DV +2) costs {cost} eb and can be done once a week. A pass tells you the company's Exposure, the trail its shortcuts and aggressive reports have left; a strong or better result also wipes some of it out.
Company.AuditCleared: Last internal audit ({date}): found Exposure {found}; the auditors cleaned some of it up, leaving it {band}.
Company.AuditFailed: Last internal audit ({date}) found nothing useful.
Company.DiligenceHint: Due diligence (Library Search or Business) on another business costs {cost} eb and can be done once a week. Name the business as you know it; a pass tells you how it stands and roughly what it is worth.

Living.Covered: The business pays their Housing and Lifestyle: {amount} eb a month, as their sheet has it.
Living.Subject: {name}: Housing and Lifestyle
Living.Body: {name} pays your Housing and Lifestyle this month: {amount} eb. Claim it from this message, then pay your rent as usual.

Kind.unmasked: Unmasked as a hidden holder of {name}
Kind.raidLost: A raid lost at {name}'s back room

Downtime.NotEnough: That takes {days} downtime day(s), and you do not have them.
Downtime.NotPrepared: You have no downtime yet: a GM has to open Crew Tools' Downtime for this character.
Downtime.AddHint: Your Crew Tools downtime goes into it.
Downtime.ExtraNote: Extra time spends a downtime day, whatever the roll.

DistrictDefs.Title: Districts from Night City Map
DistrictDefs.Hint: Districts on the map that this module has no numbers of its own for. They start from the map's danger. Traffic and rent multiply a business's takings and fixed costs, and risk how often events come; 1 is average. New businesses can choose what is on the map now, and a business in a district the map has lost keeps its name and numbers.
DistrictDefs.Name: District

Faction.Hint: Corporations and gangs a business can stand well or badly with. Link a corporation to its ticker, and give a gang the districts it holds, so the businesses there see it.

Terms.cost: Cost base from corporations in your sector: {change}.
Terms.protection: Protection money from gangs on your turf: {change}.

Faction.Name: Name
Faction.RemoveConfirm: Remove {name}? Standing with it is kept out of sight, and comes back if it is added again with the same id.
Faction.None: No factions yet: import the starter list, or add your own.
Faction.StandingHint: Each business's true standing, from -100 to 100; its owners see only the band. It fades 2 points a week toward 0, and moves at most 15 in a week, apart from what you set by hand. A gig moves it only when its GM notes make it a contract, like [NCI contract: Charter Test Clinic].

Reason.report: a regulator has been going through its monthly reports
Reason.plant: a former employee went to the regulators
Reason.blackOps: black ops were traced back to the company
Reason.story: a published story has drawn the regulators' attention
Reason.shortcuts: a shortcut went wrong, and someone noticed
Reason.unmasked: a large hidden holder was uncovered
Reason.gm: a regulator has opened a file on it

Regulator.Notice: Regulator's case: {why}. An officer must answer by {date}, or it counts as lost.
Regulator.Waiting: A regulator's case went against the company. The market is deciding the penalty.
Regulator.RollHint: One roll, against a total you cannot see: Bureaucracy, Accounting, or Bribery, which costs {bribe} eb from the company's cash whatever happens. A win clears much of the trail; a loss brings a fine and a hit to Compliance, and can be worse.
Regulator.WonNotice: The case is closed: the regulator found nothing it could use.
Regulator.LostNotice: The case went against the company. The penalty is being decided.

Mail.Open: A regulator has opened a case against {name}: {why}. An officer must answer it by {date} from the Business window, or it counts as lost.
Mail.Won: The case against {name} is closed: the regulator found nothing it could use.
Mail.Lost: The case against {name} went against the company. The penalty is being decided.
Mail.Silent: Nobody answered the case against {name} in time, so it went against the company. The penalty is being decided.
Mail.Dropped: The case against {name} has been dropped.
Mail.Fined: {name} has been fined {fine} eb, from its cash, and its Compliance has fallen.
Mail.Stopped: Its application to list has been stopped: the fee is spent, and it may apply again later.
Mail.Restated: It has had to restate its recent reports at their real figures.

Ownership.Title: Hidden ownership
Ownership.NotHidden: Your holding is on the register under your own name.
Ownership.Hidden: Your holding is hidden: {chain}. Other shareholders and the public register see {outer}.
Ownership.Fees: One more layer costs {setup} eb now, then {monthly} eb every 28 days, from your brokerage balance.
Ownership.Concealed: You hide more than 5% of a listed company: that is concealment. It draws attention each week, and NCPD Financial Crimes may look behind your layers each month; if it sees through them, you are named and fined.
Ownership.Hint: The first layer is your broker's nominee (you need a broker); after it, up to two shell companies you name. Each is a Bureaucracy or Accounting roll at DV 15: the fee is paid even if it fails, and the roll's total is how hard the layer is to see through. A layer whose monthly fee cannot be paid lapses, with every layer outside it. You still vote through your layers.
Ownership.DropConfirm: Remove your outermost layer? Its fees are not refunded, and the register will show the next layer down (or your own name).
Ownership.Found: Your digging turned something up: check your mail.
Ownership.CostDay: This takes a business day from {name}.
Ownership.CostFee: You have no business day free, so this costs {fee} eb in legwork.
Ownership.CostBribe: Bribery costs {bribe} eb more. Spent whatever you find.
Ownership.CostReason: Night City Investments: digging into a holding in {name}
Ownership.NotFound: Your digging turned up nothing this time.
Ownership.InvestigateHint: Dig into who is behind this holding: Library Search, Streetwise or Bribery, or a Netrunner's Interface. You roll against how well the layer was built, which you cannot see; a win shows you the next layer down (or who it is), a fumble tips them off. Once a week for each holding.

Mail.LapsedSubject: A layer over your holding in {name} has lapsed
Mail.Lapsed: Your brokerage balance could not cover the {fee} eb monthly fee for {layer}, your layer over your holding in {name}, so it has lapsed, with any layers outside it.
Mail.FoundSubject: What you dug up on {name}'s register
Mail.FoundLayer: Behind that holding in {name} you found another layer: {found}. Dig again to go deeper.
Mail.FoundHolder: Behind that holding in {name} you found who it is: {found}.
Mail.TippedSubject: Someone is digging into your holding in {name}
Mail.Tipped: Word reaches you that someone has been asking clumsy questions about who is behind your holding in {name}.
Mail.UnmaskedSubject: NCPD Financial Crimes: your holding in {name}
Mail.Unmasked: NCPD Financial Crimes has looked behind the layers over your {pct}% of {name} ({ticker}), above the 5% disclosure threshold. Your holding is now on the register under your own name, and you have been fined {fine} eb from your brokerage balance.

Insolvency.Banner: In administration since {date}: net assets {net} eb against debts of {debts} eb. No actions, draws, votes, new shares or buybacks until it is resolved; the weeks still close. Cash put in from the Ledger tab that lifts net assets above zero at a weekly close brings it out; otherwise the market restructures it or winds it up.

Mail.In: {name} has had more debts than assets for two weekly closes (net assets {net} eb), so it is in administration. Its owners cannot act, draw, vote or move capital until it is resolved. Cash put in that brings its net assets above zero at a weekly close ends it; otherwise it will be restructured or wound up.
Mail.Out: {name}'s net assets are above zero again, so it is out of administration and its owners can run it as before.
Mail.Restructured: {name} has been restructured: of its {debts} eb of debts, {paid} eb was paid from its cash and the rest became {shares} new shares held by its creditors, without a vote (any new shares make yours a smaller part of the company). It is out of administration.
Mail.WoundUp: {name} has been wound up. Its assets were sold; {wages} eb went to wages owed and {loans} eb to its lenders, and what was left was shared out at {perShare} eb a share, paid to you in eddies.
Mail.WoundUpListed: {name} has been wound up. Its assets were sold; {wages} eb went to wages owed and {loans} eb to its lenders, and what was left was paid at {perShare} eb a share into the brokerage balances of those holding its shares, which have left their portfolios.

Takeover.Title: Takeover offer
Takeover.Hint: A takeover offer buys the shares holders tender at its price, up to the shares it is for. NPC holders and the public float tender all their shares at a premium of 20% or more over the reference price, half at 10% to 20%, none below; the officers' defence roll moves those bars once. Holders who do not tender keep their shares.
Takeover.Awaiting: {bidder} bids {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares. The offer waits for the market's approval.
Takeover.Open: {bidder} offers {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares, a {premium}% premium on {reference} eb, until {date}.
Takeover.Defended: The officers' defence: {band}; NPC holders and the float now want {shift} points more premium.
Takeover.Mine: You have tendered {tendered} of your {held} shares.
Takeover.MineFree: You have tendered {tendered} of your {held} shares; {free} of them are free to tender (shares still locked up after the listing are not).
Takeover.Last: The last takeover offer, by {bidder} at {price} eb, closed on {date} with {shares} shares bought.
Takeover.LastControl: The last takeover offer, by {bidder} at {price} eb, closed on {date} with {shares} shares bought, giving them control.
Takeover.BidHint: Bid for a player company by its ticker: a price per share and the most shares you want. The market approves the bid first; then the whole offer is held from this brokerage balance for 7 days, and what is not spent comes back.
Takeover.BidConfirm: Bid {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares of {ticker}? Once the market approves it, {escrow} eb is held from your brokerage balance until it closes.
Takeover.BidIncomplete: Give a ticker, a price a share and how many shares.

Mail.Open: {bidder} offers {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares of {name}, a {premium}% premium, until {date}. Tender your shares, or not, from the Shareholders tab of the Business window.
Mail.Approved: Your offer of {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares of {name} is open until {date}. {escrow} eb is held from your brokerage balance.
Mail.Unfunded: Your brokerage balance could not cover the {escrow} eb your bid for {name} needs, so it has lapsed.
Mail.Rejected: The market refused your takeover bid for {name}.
Mail.ClosedSubject: The takeover offer for {name} has closed
Mail.Closed: {bidder}'s offer for {name} closed: {shares} shares bought at {price} eb. Anything you tendered has been paid into your brokerage balance.
Mail.Control: {bidder}'s offer for {name} closed: {shares} shares bought at {price} eb, and {bidder} now controls the company. Anything you tendered has been paid into your brokerage balance.
Mail.BidderClosed: Your offer for {name} closed: you bought {shares} shares at {price} eb. {refund} eb of the escrow came back to your brokerage balance.
Mail.BidderControl: Your offer for {name} closed: you bought {shares} shares at {price} eb and now control the company. {refund} eb of the escrow came back to your brokerage balance.

Capital.Title: Capital
Capital.Intro: The shareholders can vote, by a majority of the shares, to issue new shares or to buy shares back. New shares are offered to the holders at book value, each by the shares they hold now, for 14 days; what nobody takes lapses. In a buyback the company spends up to the budget from its cash buying shares at book value from any holder who sells in the next 14 days.
Capital.IntroListed: The shareholders can vote, by a majority of the shares, to sell new shares on the market or to buy shares back from it. Both need an officer's roll first.
Capital.Rights: Rights issue: {shares} new shares at {price} eb each, open until {date}; {taken} taken so far.
Capital.RightsMine: You may take {n} more, at {price} eb each.
Capital.Tender: Buyback: the company buys shares at {price} eb each until {date}; {left} eb of the budget left, {bought} bought so far.
Capital.OfferingRoll: The shareholders agreed to sell {shares} new shares on the market. An officer makes the offering roll, which sets the discount to the market price; a failure pulls the offering.
Capital.OfferingOpen: Offering {shares} new shares of {ticker} at {price} eb each, open for subscription on the market terminal until {date}; the market takes what players do not.
Capital.BuybackRoll: The shareholders agreed a buyback of up to {budget} eb. An officer times it with a roll, which sets the price it pays against the market's.
Capital.BuybackBuying: Buying back from the market each day ({adj} on the market price): {spent} of {budget} eb spent, {bought} shares bought and retired.

Dividend.Title: Dividends
Dividend.Policy: After each monthly report the company pays {pct}% of the month's real profit to its shareholders, into their brokerage accounts by the shares they hold; never more than {yield}% of the valuation in a month, nor what the cash holds, and at most {cap} eb to one holder. The market's and NPC holders' share is paid out too.
Dividend.Pending: A new payout ratio is waiting for the shareholders' votes.

Listing.Gains: Listing puts the company on the market as {ticker}: its shares trade on the terminal, the shareholders' holdings move into their brokerage portfolios (locked for 28 days), and the shares floated in the offering raise cash for the company. It takes every shareholder with a vote, naming the float (20% to 40% of the company); the listing fee is paid when you agree, whatever happens; then the market must accept the application, and two prospectus rolls must pass. The valuation is net assets plus a year of the reported profit at the {sector} sector's multiple of {multiple}; cash paid in counts only after 28 days.
Listing.Confirm: Propose listing the company? If every shareholder with a vote agrees, the listing fee is paid from its cash at once, and the application waits for the market.
Listing.Fee: The listing fee, 2% of the valuation, is {fee} eb now.
Listing.Awaiting: The shareholders have agreed to list, floating {float}% (fee {fee} eb paid). The application is waiting for the market.
Listing.Prospectus: The market has accepted the application. An officer makes each prospectus roll; both must pass.
Listing.Ready: Ready to list: {shares} new shares ({float}% of the company) offered at {price} eb a share. The offering opens on the market shortly.
Listing.Scheduled: The offering is open: {shares} new shares of {ticker} at {price} eb a share, for anyone to subscribe for on the market terminal. {ticker} lists on {date}.
Listing.Listed: Listed on the market as {ticker} since {date}, at an offer price of {price} eb. Shareholders' shares are in their brokerage portfolios, locked up until {until}; the shareholders are now whoever holds them.
Listing.Failed: A prospectus roll failed: the fee is spent. You may agree to list again from {date}.
Listing.Rejected: The market turned the application down: the fee is spent. You may agree to list again from {date}.
Listing.Review: Under the delisting review since {date}: the company's market value ({value} eb) has been too low for three reports in a row. The market may delist it, taking it private again.
Listing.LowReports: Market value below the listing floor on {n} of {of} reports in a row; at {of}, the company goes under the delisting review.
Listing.Delisted: Delisted from the market as {ticker} on {date}: the company bought back the public float and is private again.

Mail.Review: {name} ({ticker}) is worth {value} eb on the market, under the {floor} eb floor for {n} reports in a row. The market has put it under review; it may be delisted and taken private.
Mail.Delisted: {name} ({ticker}) has been delisted. The company bought the public float back; your shares have left your brokerage portfolio and are shares on its record again.

Charter.Gains: Chartering makes the business a company: three action slots a week, a Capacity ceiling of 14, shares in place of units, and later monthly reports and officers. Rent, licences and actions (DV 17) cost more. It takes every partner's agreement, naming the ticker, then three rolls any partner can make: the business plan, the registration and the capital structure. The 2,000 eb filing fee is paid when you agree, whatever happens.
Charter.SectorLine: As a company it would be in the {sector} sector.
Charter.Range: Its capital quote will be between {min} and {max} eb, depending on the capital structure roll; the business's net assets count toward it.
Charter.Confirm: Propose chartering the business? If every partner agrees, the 2,000 eb filing fee is paid from its cash at once, and the three charter rolls open.
Charter.Agreed: The partners have agreed to charter as {ticker}. Any partner may make each roll.
Charter.Awaiting: Waiting for the GM: a capital quote of {quote} eb, of which the business's net assets cover {assets} eb, leaving {shortfall} eb to pay in.
Charter.AwaitingCovered: Waiting for the GM: a capital quote of {quote} eb, covered in full by the business's net assets ({assets} eb), so nothing is paid in.
Charter.Funding: The GM has approved the charter. Pay in {shortfall} eb by {date} ({paid} eb so far, at most {max} eb): each payment buys shares at book value. The company is formed when it is met.
Charter.Refused: The capital structure roll failed, so the charter was refused. You can agree to try again from {date}.
Charter.Rejected: The GM turned the charter down; anything paid in was refunded.
Charter.Lapsed: The funding window ran out; everything paid in was refunded.
Charter.Kept: Kept for the next try (30 days): {parts}.

GMSyndicate.Title: Player syndicates
GMSyndicate.Intro: Each syndicate's members, its account and what is waiting. You can pass or veto any proposal, and close a syndicate whose account holds nothing but cash (it is paid out by units).
GMSyndicate.Disabled: Player syndicates are switched off in the module settings. Existing syndicates keep their holdings.
GMSyndicate.RejectConfirm: Turn this syndicate down? Nothing has been paid in yet, so it is simply removed.
GMSyndicate.CloseConfirm: Close this syndicate? Its cash is paid into the members' brokerage balances by units, and it stops trading.
GMSyndicate.CloseLater: To close it, its account must first hold nothing but cash.
GMSyndicate.Money: Cash {cash} eb · value {total} eb · {nav} eb a unit · officers' limit {limit} eb a day each

Production.GMHint: What each kind of business can make. The defaults come from the system's compendiums; drop an item in the box to add another, from a compendium or the Items directory. Items marked illegal need an open back room to make (a company needs none), and can only be sold by fencing. With the underworld setting off, nobody can make them.
Production.Benches: {benches} bench(es), each with 7 days of work a week. At this stage the business can make items up to {top}.
Production.NoWorkshop: No workshop yet. Build one on the Projects tab.
Production.LineTerms: {tier}, DV {dv}: up to {size} a run, {materials} eb of materials each, market price {price} eb.
Production.RunGoing: On the benches: {count} × {name}, about {weeks} more week(s) after this one's close.
Production.MakerRuns: Your Maker runs the line in any week no partner does.
Production.NoMaker: With no Maker on the staff, the line only runs when a partner takes the week's action.
Production.StoreCap: Items that do not stack: {loose} of {cap} the storeroom holds.
Production.SellsAt: The shop sells it at {price} eb
Production.NotForShop: Illegal: only a fence takes it, at {price} eb
Production.IllegalLine: Illegal: off the books, paid from dirty cash first, and each run adds Exposure.
Production.FenceTerms: Pays {price}% of market price, off the books.
Production.SalesNote: The shop sells stock at the week's close, up to about {limit} eb a week as things stand, dearest first. Unused limit carries over: {saved} eb saved so far, up to {most} eb.
Production.ConsignHint: Consign items from your own sheet: they stay yours until they sell, and you get the sale price less the shop's 30%. Take them back any time.
Production.ConsignDrop: Drop an item from your sheet here

Project.Intro: Projects improve the premises. The partners agree on one (a majority of the votes) and it is paid from the cash at once; then they finish it with business days, 3 each a week, which lapse when the week closes. One project at a time.
Project.IntroCompany: Projects improve the premises. The shareholders agree on one (a majority of the shares) and it is paid from the cash at once; then they finish it with business days, 3 each a week, which lapse when the week closes. One project at a time.

Hint.backRoom: An illegal operation behind the shop. Off the books, its takings are dirty cash, and it carries risk. Not at a chartered company.
Hint.expansion: A second chair, a bigger bay: more room to do business.
Hint.refit: New kit and better suppliers: cheaper to run.
Hint.security: Locks, cameras, a reinforced door: less protection money, fewer break-ins.
Hint.storefront: A refurbished front and signage: people notice.
Hint.staffRoom: A break room and lockers: room for one more, and happier staff.
Hint.workshop: Benches and tools, to make what the shop sells.

Effect.Label: What it does
Effect.expansion: Capacity {now} → {after} (the ceiling at this stage is {cap}).
Effect.refit: Cost base {now} → {after}; it creeps back up week by week.
Effect.security: Level {level} of {max} (protection money −{cut}% now): each level cuts it a further 25% and halves break-ins.
Effect.securityNone: No upgrade yet (up to {max} levels): each level cuts protection money by 25% and halves break-ins.
Effect.storefront: Reputation +{rep} at once, and from then on it settles toward {target} rather than 50. Once a stage.
Effect.storefrontAgain: Reputation +{rep} at once. Once a stage.
Effect.staffRoom: One more place for staff ({places} now), and paid weeks lift NPC staff loyalty to {cap}. Once a stage.
Effect.workshop: {benches} bench(es), up to {top} items. Once a stage: built again after stepping up, it has more.

Result.Label: Result
Result.backRoom: A back room, behind the shop

Project.CapacityNext: (the hatched part: what the next expansion adds)
Project.CapacityFull: (at this stage's ceiling: step up to grow further)
Project.NoCrew: Nobody has put days in yet.
Project.AddHint: Your business days this week go into it.
Project.NeedsCash: Needs {cost} eb; the cash holds {till} eb.
Project.OneAtATime: One project at a time: the next can be proposed once this one is finished.
Project.Pending: A project is waiting for the partners' votes on the Partners tab.

Rumour.Subject: Rumour: {name}

move.typical: People are talking about {name}. The word is its price is heading {way}.
move.substantial: People are talking about {name}. The word is its price is heading {way}, on account of {why}.
move.detailed: A good source on {name} ({ticker}): its price moves {way} about {percent}% within {days} day(s), on account of {why}.

press.vague: Someone has been asking questions about {name}.
press.typical: A reporter is digging into {name}. There's a story on the way.
press.detailed: A good source: {outlet} prints {story} about {name} in about {days} day(s).

hidden.vague: Someone's being very quiet about what they own in {name}.
hidden.typical: There's a hidden stake in {name}, held behind a front.
hidden.substantial: There's a hidden stake of over 5% in {name}, held behind a front.

BackRoom.NoneYet: This business has no back room. Opening one is a project: see the Projects tab.
BackRoom.Pending: Finished, and waiting for the GM before it opens.
BackRoom.TakeHint: No limit, but every {every} eb taken adds {exposure} Exposure. Dirty cash is lost if the business closes.

BackRoom.Last: Last week: {earned} eb earned, {laundered} eb laundered, {paid} eb in pay-offs.
BackRoom.LastSupply: Last week: {earned} eb earned, {supply} eb of it on supplies, {laundered} eb laundered, {paid} eb in pay-offs.

Trouble.fightPit: A fight goes too far, on camera
Trouble.fixersRoom: A fixer wants a meeting kept off the books
Trouble.identityForgery: A customer is caught with your work
Trouble.illegalMods: A gun is traced back to you
Trouble.hotGoods: A driver is stopped and talks
Trouble.peopleRunning: A run goes wrong in public
Trouble.launderette: A client's money has been followed

Trouble.counterfeits: A run of fakes falls apart
Trouble.streetDealing: A bad batch hits the block

Trouble.bootlegs: A bad copy burns a customer
Trouble.paidStories: A patron wants a story run
Trouble.protection: A client wants more than protection

BackRoom.FavourNeeds: Needs friendly standing or better with {name}.

steady.Name: Steady
steady.Hint: Earns and draws attention as a back room usually does.

loud.Name: Loud
loud.Hint: Earns half as much again, and the roll swings it further. Half as much Exposure again, and a quarter more raids.

quiet.Name: Quiet
quiet.Hint: Earns about two thirds, more evenly. Half the Exposure, and half the raids.

hungry.Name: Hungry
hungry.Hint: Earns half as much again, but a quarter of it goes on supplies, out of the dirty cash. A quarter more Exposure.

connected.Name: Connected
connected.Hint: Earns half. Less Exposure, and each week worked lifts standing with a faction you choose.

laundering.Name: Laundering
laundering.Hint: Earns four fifths, with less Exposure, and can launder twice as much a week.

BackRoom.LastLow: Last week you lay low. {laundered} eb laundered, {paid} eb in pay-offs.
BackRoom.Shut: Shut by a raid. It can be built again as a project.
BackRoom.ShutForGood: Shut by a raid, for good. A chartered company can't build another.
BackRoom.RaidShutForGood: The raid on {name} shut the back room for good: {seized} eb seized and a {fine} eb fine. The company carries on.
BackRoom.Offer: {gang} offers {cash} eb for {cut}% of the back room's takings, at least {minimum} eb a week. It would charge no protection and send no shakedowns.
BackRoom.Deal: {gang} has a deal: {cut}% of the takings, for {cash} eb put in. No protection money or shakedowns from them.
BackRoom.DealUnpaid: {gang} has a deal: {cut}% of the takings, for {cash} eb put in. Last week's cut could not be paid, and they noticed.
BackRoom.DealHint: Needs the gang at neutral or better.
BackRoom.TakeDeal: Put the offer to the partners
BackRoom.DealEnded: {gang} has walked away from its deal with {name}, and keeps what it put in.
BackRoom.InformantFound: Your money found out who has been talking: {name}.
BackRoom.AuditInformant: Last internal audit ({date}): someone on the staff has been talking: {name}.
BackRoom.RaidIfNot: Unanswered, they seize all the dirty cash, fine the business and shut the back room, and every partner draws heat.
BackRoom.RaidWon: The raid on {name} found nothing it could use. Some of the heat is off.
BackRoom.RaidLost: The raid on {name} found the back room's money: {seized} eb seized and a {fine} eb fine. The room is still running.
BackRoom.RaidShut: The raid on {name} shut the back room: {seized} eb seized and a {fine} eb fine. The shop carries on.

Scene.Mail: {event} at {name}: this one is going to be settled in person. Talk to your GM.
Scene.MailWon: {name} came out of it well. Word gets round, and Reputation is up a little.
Scene.MailLost: {name} came off worse. The damage is in the books.

Hook.sabotage: {faction} wants {name} out of action. Someone is in {place} tonight, after hours, with tools and bad intentions. Catch them, follow them, or cut a deal.
Hook.smear: {faction} is paying for dirt on {name}. A journalist with a story and a deadline turns up at {place} asking for a comment, and someone has fed them. Who, and what do they have?
Hook.bust: A raid hits {place}, looking for the {room} behind {name}. Someone has been talking. Hide it, bribe it, fight it or run.
Hook.raid: Inspectors are on their way to {place}, tipped off by {faction}, and they know where to look. The crew has an hour to clean up, bluff it out or lean on someone.
Hook.poaching: {faction} wants {staff} away from {name}, and has made an offer with a threat behind it. Meet {staff}, meet their handler, or make a better case.
Hook.shakedown: {faction} has had enough of {name}. A crew arrives at {place}, armed and in no mood to talk, for more than the usual cut.
Hook.collectors: Collectors arrive at {place} for what {name} owes, and they've brought friends. Pay, talk, or make them regret it.
Hook.grudge: An employee {name} let go is back at {place} with friends, and a list of what they're owed.

Jobs.None: No roles are open right now.
Jobs.BoardHint: Roles open at companies around the city. Applying is one roll with your own skill, and you can try each company once a week. The wage is a guide: what you're paid depends on your skills and how the interview goes.
Jobs.Title: Apply to be {post} at {name}
Jobs.Hint: A roll against DV {dv}. Pass, and your application goes in. A better roll earns a better wage if you're taken on.
Jobs.Subject: Your application to {name}
Jobs.Hired: {name} has taken you on as {post}, at {wage} eb a week. You start now: see Your jobs in the Business window.
Jobs.Turned: {name} won't be taking you on as {post}. You can try them again in a week.
Jobs.ShiftHint: A roll against DV {dv}, once a week for all your jobs. A pass earns a bonus and the boss notices; a failure or a missed week doesn't go unnoticed either.
Jobs.Warned: You've been warned: the boss isn't happy. Another poor week and you're out.
Jobs.WarnedMail: A word from {name}: your work hasn't been good enough. Turn things around this week, or you're finished here.
Jobs.Sacked: {name} has let you go. You're paid {paid} eb in lieu of notice.
Jobs.Promoted: {name} is pleased with you: your pay goes up to {wage} eb a week.

Payslip.Bonus: A bonus for your shift: {bonus} eb, making {total} eb in all.

Jobs.NoJobs: No jobs yet. The Jobs tab in the market window lists the companies hiring.

Run.Title: Run a story
Run.Hint: Runs now, whatever the chance, with no approval. Nothing needs to be true. It ignores the limit of one story in 28 days, and starts it. A business with an event this week gets it as next week's event.
Run.HeadlineHint: Leave empty for the usual headline
Run.Next: This week already has an event, so the story will be next week's.

Reason.press-queued: That business already has a story waiting for next week.
Reason.press-busy: That character already has a story running.
Reason.press-no-stake: That character has no concealed stake in a listed company.
Reason.press-no-heat: Stories about characters need heat tracking on.
Reason.press-no-underworld: A crime expose needs Underworld content on.
Reason.press-bad-kind: That kind of story doesn't fit that target. Pick one from the matching group.

Reason.no-target: Choose who the story is about.

Angle.money: A reporter is calling round about your finances, and someone is talking.
Angle.crime: A reporter has been watching who comes and goes, and wants a comment on what goes on here.
Angle.service: A reporter is collecting complaints from your customers.
Angle.smear: A reporter has an ugly story about you and doesn't seem to care if it's true.
Angle.dirty: A reporter has been asking who tipped you off, and how you've done so well out of it.
Angle.hidden: A reporter has been following the money behind a company you'd rather not be linked to.

Headline.crime: {outlet}: what is really going on at {name}?

Why.money: It has lost money lately or its compliance is poor.
Why.crime: Its Exposure is moderate or higher, or it was raided recently.
Why.service: Its Reputation is poor, or it has had an accident or a stock query.
Why.smear: Nothing true is needed: it's harder to believe.
Why.smearCharacter: Nothing true is needed: it's harder to believe.
Why.dirty: Their heat has been noticed or higher lately.
Why.hidden: They hold a concealed stake in a listed company. The headline names the company, not them.

Mail.Subject: The story about {name}
Mail.Ignored: The story {outlet} ran about {name} went nowhere. Nobody believed it.
Mail.Answered: People believed the story {outlet} ran about {name}, but your answer killed it. No harm done.
Mail.Halved: People believed the story {outlet} ran about {name}, and your answer only took the edge off. It cost you, though not as much as it might have.
Mail.Full: People believed the story {outlet} ran about {name}, and nothing stopped it. It cost you in full.

Char.Subject: A reporter is asking about {name}
Char.Told: {outlet} is running a story. You have {days} days to answer it, from the Pending tab of your Business window. It prints in a few days, and silence will cost you most if it sticks.
Char.Title: Answer {outlet}
Char.Hint: A roll against DV {dv}. A pass stops any harm, and a failure halves it. You won't know until the end whether anyone believed the story.
Char.Ignored: The story {outlet} ran went nowhere. Nobody believed it.
Char.Answered: People believed the story {outlet} ran, but your answer killed it. No harm done.
Char.Halved: People believed the story {outlet} ran, and your answer only took the edge off.
Char.Full: People believed the story {outlet} ran, and nothing stopped it. It cost you in full.

Story.Title: A story about {name}
Story.Hint: The public believes it on 1d10 of {base} or under, without Luck. Any evidence adds {bonus}, and more than {many} pieces add {manyBonus}. Your rank moves the price up to {cap}%. You can publish once a week, and another story about the same company within 30 days needs new evidence.
Story.Headline: Headline (optional)
Story.NoEvidence: You hold no unused evidence about this company.
Story.Believed: The public buys your story (rolled {die}, needed {target} or under).
Story.BelievedWaiting: The public would buy your story (rolled {die}, needed {target} or under). It waits for the GM.
Story.NotBelieved: Nobody buys your story (rolled {die}, needed {target} or under).

Story.EvidenceHint: Put a piece of evidence about a company in a character's inventory, for a Media's story. A successful investigation or due diligence makes one by itself.

GMBusiness.CharterRejectConfirm: Turn this charter down? Anything the partners paid in is refunded; the filing fee is not.

GMBusiness.Title: Player businesses
GMBusiness.Intro: Every business at every stage, with its true state, Exposure included. Players see their own businesses only, as bands rather than numbers.
GMBusiness.RejectConfirm: Turn this business down? Every partner gets their share of the money back.

Corp.Title: Jobs at market corporations
Corp.Hint: Give a market company jobs for player characters: they apply from the Jobs tab of the market window, or you offer one here. Wages come from outside the game's economy, as the company's books aren't in play; a shift earns a bonus and standing as at an NPC's company. An employee trading the company's shares counts as an insider when a gig opens a window on it.
Corp.KindHint: The kind gives each post its skills: a security outfit's floor works with Tactics or Persuasion, a clinic's with Cybertech or Paramedic. A role with no places is closed.
Corp.Dv: DV to apply and work a shift
Corp.Gone: This company is no longer on the market. Its jobs carry on until you remove them.
Corp.RemoveConfirm: Everyone working for this company is let go with a week's pay, and its jobs come off the board.
Corp.DismissConfirm: Let this employee go, with a week's pay?
Corp.NoCompanies: Every market company has jobs set up already, or there are none.

Npc.Title: New NPC company
Npc.Hint: A company owned and run by one of your NPCs. It opens at once and runs itself each week. To step in, open it and act as the owner: anything you do is left alone, and it fills in the rest when the week closes. The profile only changes what it does from the registered stage up, as a side business has one action a week.
Npc.Name: Name
Npc.Held: Owned by {name}. The GM is running it.

Reason.bad-owner: Search for an NPC and pick one from the list. It can't be a player's character.

Reason.ticker-taken: That ticker is already in use.
Reason.not-npc: That business isn't run by an NPC.

GMBusiness.LeavesHint: For a character who has died or left the table: the buy-out rule applies to their stake.
GMBusiness.RemoveConfirm: Delete this business's record for good? No money moves.
GMBusiness.SetupFailed: Setup roll {band}: can be tried again (range {range}).
GMBusiness.CampaignWaiting: A {kind} against {name} ({ticker}), run {date}: {percent}% on its share price. Let it run or stop it; the cost stays spent.
GMBusiness.BigEvent: A big event this week: {event}. Run it as a scene, or leave it as a roll. {hook}
GMBusiness.RoomPending: A back room is ready to open: {kind}. Let it open or turn it down; what it cost stays spent.
GMBusiness.RoomOpen: Back room: {kind}, {dirty} eb of dirty cash.
GMBusiness.RoomShut: Back room: {kind}, shut by a raid.
GMBusiness.RoomDeal: A deal with {gang}: {cut}% of the back room's takings.
GMBusiness.StaffOffer: {name}, an NPC, is offered a job as {post} at {wage} eb a week. Answer for them.
GMBusiness.TeamLoyaltyHint: A team member's Loyalty, 0 to 10. Set it for what happened at the table: the rulebook's other gains and losses.
GMBusiness.ListingRejectConfirm: Turn this listing down? The listing fee is not refunded; they may agree again in 14 days.
GMBusiness.DelistConfirm: Delist this company? It buys the market's shares back at the market price from its cash (borrowing from the bank what it lacks), the shareholders' shares leave their portfolios and become shares on its record again, and it goes back to being a private company. This cannot be undone.
GMBusiness.CaseNotice: Regulator's case: {why}. An officer may answer until {date}. Exposure {exposure}.
GMBusiness.CaseLost: Regulator's case lost ({how}): {why}. Proposed fine {fine} eb and Compliance -10.{more}
GMBusiness.CaseSerious: Serious: a listing application stops, or the last three reports are restated.
GMBusiness.Administration: In administration since {date}: net assets {net} eb (loans {loans} eb, wages owed {wages} eb, overdraft {overdraft} eb). Restructure it or wind it up; cash its owners put in that lifts net assets above zero at a close ends it by itself.
GMBusiness.RestructureConfirm: Restructure this company? Its cash pays what it can of the owed wages and loans, keeping four weeks of upkeep; the rest (and any overdraft) is written off for new shares at half its book value per share, held by its creditors without a vote, diluting the old holders. Reputation and Compliance drop by 10. It leaves administration.
GMBusiness.WindUpConfirm: Wind this company up? Its assets sell at half their book value; owed wages are paid first, then the loans, then the holders by shares (a listed company's into brokerage balances, its shares leaving portfolios). The business closes. This cannot be undone.

Takeover.awaiting: Takeover bid by {bidder}: {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares ({escrow} eb, held from their brokerage balance when approved).
Takeover.open: Takeover offer by {bidder} open until {date}: {price} eb a share for up to {shares} shares; {tendered} tendered by players so far.

Listing.awaiting: Listing as {ticker} waiting for you: valuation {valuation} eb, float {float}%. Hidden Exposure {exposure}.
Listing.prospectus: Listing as {ticker} approved: the prospectus rolls are under way.
Listing.ready: Listing as {ticker} ready: {shares} shares at {price} eb; the market company is being made.
Listing.scheduled: Listing as {ticker} scheduled: {shares} shares at {price} eb, the offering open on the market until the listing day.

Event.FromGang: It's {faction}. Beating them with force (Combat Awareness, Backup or security staff) works, but they won't forget it.

sabotage.Name: Sabotage
sabotage.Hint: Someone has been at the equipment overnight, and it wasn't an accident.

roomNoise.Name: Too much noise
roomNoise.Hint: The back room drew a crowd, and someone filmed it.
roomNoise.IfNot: Unanswered, it adds Exposure and hurts the shop's Reputation.

roomLooseEnd.Name: A loose end
roomLooseEnd.Hint: A customer of the back room is talking.
roomLooseEnd.IfNot: Unanswered, it adds a lot of Exposure.

roomBadBatch.Name: A bad batch
roomBadBatch.IfNot: Unanswered, the room earns nothing this week and the shop's Reputation suffers.

roomFavour.Name: A favour asked
roomFavour.Hint: The faction behind the back room wants something done.
roomFavour.IfNot: Unanswered, your standing with them falls.

roomBooks.Name: The books don't add up
roomBooks.Hint: The back room's money has left a trail.
roomBooks.IfNot: Unanswered, it adds Exposure and costs a quarter of the dirty cash.

roomRival.Name: A rival operation
roomRival.Hint: Another crew is moving in on the back room's trade.
roomRival.IfNot: Unanswered, the room's earnings are halved this week and Exposure rises.

roomBigOrder.Name: An offer you can't refuse
roomBigOrder.Hint: A big order, from someone you'd rather not owe. Taking it adds Exposure, whether or not the job goes well, and pays in dirty cash if it does.

bust.Name: A raid on the back room
bust.Hint: They've come for what's behind the shop, and they aren't leaving without a look.

press.Name: A reporter asking questions
press.IfNot: If the story is believed and goes unanswered, it costs you in full. Answering well stops it, and answering badly halves it.

smear.Name: A smear campaign
smear.Hint: Ugly stories about the business are doing the rounds, and someone is paying for them.

raid.Name: A tipped-off raid
raid.Hint: Inspectors are on the way, and they seem to know exactly where to look.

shakedown.Name: A shakedown
shakedown.Hint: A gang wants protection money on top of what you already pay.

theft.Name: A break-in
theft.Hint: Someone has been through the stock overnight, and they will be back.

breakdown.Name: Something breaks
breakdown.Hint: The kit the business runs on has given out.

shortage.Name: A supply shortage
shortage.Hint: The usual supplier cannot deliver this week.

rival.Name: A rival opens nearby
rival.Hint: A competitor is undercutting you and talking you down.

collectors.Name: Debt collectors
collectors.Hint: The fixer wants the payment you missed, and has sent people to make the point.

trouble.Name: Trouble with a customer
trouble.Hint: A customer, or a job, has gone wrong in a way people will talk about.

inspection.Name: An inspection
inspection.Hint: The city's inspectors want to see the books and the licences.

windfall.Name: A big order
windfall.Hint: Someone with money wants something done this week, if you can deliver.

grudge.Name: An old grudge
grudge.Hint: Someone you let go has come back with friends to make a point.

sickDay.Name: Off sick
sickDay.IfNot: If nobody sees to it, {name}'s post does nothing this week.

lightFingers.Name: Light fingers
lightFingers.Hint: Stock and cash have been going missing, and it looks like an inside job.
lightFingers.IfNot: If nobody looks into it, 5% to 15% of the week's takings walk out of the door. Catch the thief and they can be let go without severance.

payDispute.Name: A pay dispute
payDispute.Hint: The staff say they are not paid enough, and they mean to stop work.
payDispute.IfNot: If nobody talks them round (or pays every employee a bonus this week), the staff down tools for the week and lose loyalty.

poaching.Name: A poaching offer
poaching.Hint: A rival has offered {name} a better job.
poaching.IfNot: If nobody makes the case to stay (or gives a raise of 10% or more this week), {name} leaves, unless devoted to you.

accident.Name: An accident at work
accident.Hint: {name} has been hurt on the job.
accident.IfNot: If nobody patches them up, the business pays the medical bills and {name} is out for this week and the next.

starTurn.Name: A star turn
starTurn.Hint: One of the staff has done something people are talking about.
starTurn.IfNot: Make the most of it and Reputation rises; otherwise the moment passes.

doubleBooked.Name: Double-booked
doubleBooked.Hint: {name} is wanted at their other job this week as well.
doubleBooked.IfNot: If nobody persuades {name} to work your shifts, they work the other job this week and do nothing here.

fullTimeOffer.Name: A full-time offer
fullTimeOffer.Hint: {name}'s other employer wants them full time.
fullTimeOffer.IfNot: If nobody makes the case to stay (or gives a raise of 10% or more this week), {name} leaves to work there full time.

talkingShop.Name: Talking shop
talkingShop.Hint: {name} has been talking about this place at their other job.
talkingShop.IfNot: If nobody finds out what was said, the other business learns how this one stands. Caught well, you learn about them instead.

Settled.passed: Agreed at once: your units carried it, and it has been done.
Settled.void: Agreed, but it could not be done: {reason}
Settled.open: Over your limit: sent to the members for a vote.

Syndicate.Title: Syndicate: {name}

Syndicate.LimitLeft: You have {left} eb of today's limit left.
Syndicate.LeaveConfirm: Leaving redeems all your units at the value per unit on the day they are paid, after the market's settlement delay, and then takes you off the members' list. Leave the syndicate?

role.member: Make {name} a member again, no longer an officer

Proposal.limit: Set the officers' limit to {amount} eb an order

business.buyout: Buy a stake in {name} for about {amount} eb

Proposal.dissolve: Dissolve the syndicate and pay out its cash by units

Business.Title: Business
Business.StartHint: Found another business with this character.
Business.Disabled: Player businesses are turned off in the module settings.
Business.NoCharacter: You have no character to run a business with.
Business.StartIntro: A side business needs no charter: a stall, a garage bay, a back-room clinic. Put in what eddies and gear you have, invite any partners, and once everyone has answered, any partner makes the setup roll.
Business.Name: Name
Business.LocationHint: e.g. a back room in Watson
Business.GearDrop: Gear you bring (optional): drag an item here from your character's sheet, the Items directory or a compendium. Its book value is its market price.
Business.GearLeaves: leaves your sheet; back if the business never opens

Business.SweatHint: An optional slice of units for the partner who will do most of the work. Decisions follow units; closing the business, and changing the agreement, need every partner.

Business.AwaitingGM: Everything is ready. The GM has to approve the business before it opens.
Business.Escrow: Money in, held until it opens
