Business.SetupFailed: Setup roll: {band}. You can try again from {date}.
Business.Shortfall: {amount} eb more is needed before it can open.
Business.TopUpHint: Eddies go into the business's cash and gear into the fit-out. Nobody's units change, so every holder's stake gains in proportion; you are not given a bigger share for it.
Business.TopUpHintCompany: Eddies go into the company's cash and gear into the fit-out. Nobody's shares change, so every holder's stake gains in proportion; you are not given a bigger share for it.
Business.WithdrawConfirm: Take your share of the money back out and leave the business before it opens?
Business.WeekRuns: This operating week runs from {from} and closes at the first market tick on or after {to} ({day}).
Business.HelpHint: A complementary check: no slot, and on a success the partner who takes this action gets +1. One check a week each.
Business.HelpHintCompany: A complementary check: no slot, and on a success the officer who takes this action gets +1. One check a week each.
Business.AlreadyHelped: This character has already made a complementary check this week.
Business.UnworkedNote: A week nobody works the shop still trades, at a little under the usual takings. Reputation drifts back toward the district's usual and costs creep up when nobody looks after them.

fence.Name: Fence stock
fence.Hint: Trading, Streetwise or Operator: sells stock off the books, illegal goods first. The roll sets how much, and it adds Exposure.

produce.Name: Run the line
produce.Hint: With the trade's skills or Maker, at the book's DV for the item: how many come out sellable.

work.Name: Work the shop
work.Hint: With the trade's skills: sets the week's takings.

promote.Name: Promote
promote.Hint: Persuasion, Wardrobe & Style, Composition, Credibility or Charismatic Impact: Reputation and foot traffic up.

source.Name: Source supplies
source.Hint: Trading, Streetwise or Operator: the Cost base down.

fixUp.Name: Fix the place up
fixUp.Hint: Basic Tech or Maker: Capacity up, so more takings are possible.

keepSafe.Name: Keep it safe
keepSafe.Hint: Tactics, Persuasion, Combat Awareness or Backup: less protection money this week.

court.Name: Court a client
court.Hint: Business, Persuasion, Trading, Operator, Charismatic Impact or Credibility: raises standing with a corporation.

respects.Name: Pay respects
respects.Hint: Streetwise, Persuasion, Operator or Charismatic Impact: raises standing with a gang.

bigNight.Name: A big night
bigNight.Hint: With the room's own skills, in place of the week's work: half as much dirty cash again on a pass, and twice the Exposure from work whatever the roll. Once in 28 days.

coverTrail.Name: Cover the trail
coverTrail.Hint: With the room's own skills: earns nothing, costs nothing, and sheds Exposure on a pass.

newSupplier.Name: Find a new supplier
newSupplier.Hint: With the room's own skills: on a pass, supplies cost 15% of what it earns instead of 25% for four weeks. On a failure, a bad batch is twice as likely for as long. Once in 28 days.

callFavour.Name: Call in a favour
callFavour.Hint: With the room's own skills, at friendly or better with its faction: on a pass, spends 5 standing to stop this week's shakedown, or to shed 5 Exposure if there is none.

clientWash.Name: Wash for a client
clientWash.Hint: With the room's own skills: earns a fee in dirty cash, and leaves traces as laundering does. Once in 28 days.

roomWork.Name: Work the back room
roomWork.Hint: With its own skills: dirty cash, off the books. It always adds some Exposure, and more on a poor roll.

launder.Name: Launder
launder.Hint: Accounting or Business (Bribery at DV +2): moves dirty cash into the business's cash, up to 30% of the week's takings. A poor roll leaves traces, and a bookkeeper helps.

payOff.Name: Pay someone off
payOff.Hint: Bribery: cuts Exposure, paid from the dirty cash. A fumble makes it worse.

dealGang.Name: Deal with a gang
dealGang.Hint: Streetwise, Persuasion or Operator: a gang on your turf offers money for a cut of the back room, and leaves you alone. It won't talk if it's wary or hostile.

dumping.Name: Dump the waste
dumping.Hint: Business (Trading at DV +2) or Operator: the biggest lift to the takings, and the most Exposure. A fumble is a scandal.

bribeRegulator.Name: Bribe a regulator
bribeRegulator.Hint: Bribery or Operator: cuts Exposure, and a good roll makes an open case easier to answer.

blackOps.Name: Black ops
blackOps.Hint: Tactics, Streetwise, Operator or Interface: hits another company's share price harder than a campaign. One a month, shared with campaigns. If it's traced back, it's a scandal and a regulator's case.

supply.Name: Supply contract
supply.Hint: Moto, and a Nomad's contacts on the roads: running costs down by up to 10% for four weeks. A fumble loses the shipment.

venue.Name: Gig at the venue
venue.Hint: Charismatic Impact: this week's takings and Reputation up, most of all at a bar or club.

campaign.Name: Run a campaign
campaign.Hint: A smear (Composition or Persuasion) or a leak (Library Search or Interface) against a listed company: its share price falls a little. One a month.

contracts.Name: Chase contracts
contracts.Hint: Business (Persuasion or Trading at DV +2), Teamwork, Operator or Maker: sets the week's takings, and Reputation up a little.

books.Name: Tighten the books
books.Hint: Accounting (Business at DV +2) or Moto: the Cost base down.

relations.Name: Investor relations
relations.Hint: Trading (Persuasion or Wardrobe & Style at DV +2), Credibility or Charismatic Impact: Reputation up.

permits.Name: Permits and compliance
permits.Hint: Bureaucracy (Local Expert or Persuasion at DV +2) or Backup: Compliance up, and less protection money this week.

shortcuts.Name: Shortcuts
shortcuts.Hint: Bribery (Streetwise at DV +2) or Operator: the biggest lift to the takings, but it always leaves a trail (Exposure), and a fumble costs Compliance.

Business.CloseConfirmCompany: Propose closing the company? If every shareholder with a vote agrees, the gear is sold for half its value, stock counts at what it cost, consigned items go back to their owners, and everything is paid out by shares.

Business.LeaveConfirmCompany: Offer your shares to the other shareholders? They have the buy-out window to buy them at book value; after that they go to your heir.
Business.DecisionsHint: Closing needs every partner with a vote; one refusal ends the proposal.
Business.DecisionsHintCompany: Closing needs every shareholder with a vote; one refusal ends the proposal.

Business.FixerTerms: A fixer lends up to {limit} eb with no questions asked, at {rate}% a week, repaid over {weeks} weeks. A missed payment costs a late fee and Reputation, and the fixer's collectors come calling. It needs a majority of the voting units.

Business.AngelIntroCompany: An angel is an outside backer. Staff.Title: Staff
Staff.Intro: Employees work in the business for a wage. Each holds a role, and their skills for that role set what they do for the business and what they are paid.
Staff.RejectConfirm: Turn this applicant away? They leave the list for good.
Staff.Offered: Job offer made, waiting for response
Staff.OfferedNpc: Job offer made, waiting for response
Staff.FireConfirm: Propose letting this employee go? It needs a majority, and an employee who has started is paid a week's wage.
Staff.OvertimeHint: Call an employee in for any of this week's rolls from the roll dialog: half a week's wage to take a slot or answer an event, a quarter to help. Two shifts each a week. Employees cannot use Luck or business days.

PostHint.floor: The trade's own skills (role abilities that fit it count higher): lifts the takings, more with a higher base. No more on the floor than the Capacity allows.
PostHint.maker: The trade's skills or Maker: runs the workshop's line in any week no partner does.
PostHint.manager: Business, or the trade's skills a level lower: works the shop (at a company, chases contracts) in any week no partner does. One per business.
PostHint.security: Tactics, Brawling, Handgun, Melee Weapon or Human Perception (Combat Awareness and Backup count higher): answers a shakedown, break-in or trouble no partner answers.
PostHint.bookkeeper: Accounting, or Business a level lower: trims the Cost base each week, and gives a company's monthly report its +1. From registration.
PostHint.sales: Business, Persuasion or Trading: lifts the takings by half what a floor hand does, and keeps Reputation nearer 55. Companies only.
PostHint.publicist: Composition, Wardrobe & Style or Persuasion (Credibility and Charismatic Impact count higher): Reputation up each week. Companies only.
PostHint.compliance: Bureaucracy or Local Expert: Compliance up each week, and answers an inspection no partner answers. Companies only.
PostHint.hand: The trade's skills: works the back room when no partner does. Paid half as much again, and adds to the risk of a raid. Knows what goes on there, so loyalty matters.
PostHint.launderer: Accounting or Business: washes the dirty cash when no partner does. Paid half as much again, and adds to the risk of a raid. Knows what goes on there, so loyalty matters.
PostHint.fixer: Bribery or Streetwise: at moderate Exposure or higher, pays people off from the dirty cash when no partner does; at a company, bribes the regulator from the cash if there is no dirty money to use, as long as 5,000 eb would be left. Paid half as much again, and adds to the risk of a raid.

Staff.RecruitHint: Fill a role from its Hire button: a character (a player character, or an NPC tagged staff or employee in Night City Messenger), or advertise the job, a Business, Streetwise or Library Search roll at this stage's DV costing {cost} eb, once a week. A good advert brings up to three applicants, better skilled and asking less; a poor one fewer and dearer. Applicants wait 7 days. The going rate is {rate} eb a week for each point of skill.
Staff.NoOpenPost: Every place is taken: no role is open.
Staff.CandidateTerms: Going rate {rate} eb a week. Waits until {date}.
Staff.HireCharacterHint: A player character, or an NPC linked to a Night City Messenger contact tagged staff or employee. Hiring needs a majority; then a player character accepts from their own window, and the GM answers for an NPC. Pay is a share of the going rate, 80% to 150%.
Staff.RateHint: The going rate here is {rate} eb a week for each point of the base for the role.
Staff.Pending: A decision about staff is waiting for votes on the Partners tab.
Staff.JobsHint: Your wage is paid into your eddies when the business's week closes. The partners may call you in for overtime.
Staff.QuitConfirm: Quit this job? There is no severance when you leave.
Staff.DropHint: Or drag a character from the Actors directory here to propose hiring them for this role, at this pay.
Staff.DropActorOnly: Only a character can be hired.
Staff.DropConfirm: Propose hiring {name} as {post} at {pct}% of the going rate? It needs a majority of the votes.
Staff.CannotHire: Only a partner who can act for the business can hire.
Staff.AdvertiseHint: Advertise the job: a Business, Streetwise or Library Search roll at this stage's DV, costing {cost} eb, once a week. The better the roll, the more applicants (up to three), the better their skill and the less they ask. A new advert replaces the applicants still waiting for this role. Each applicant is hired on the wage they ask.
Staff.ApplicantTerms: Asks {wage} eb a week ({pct}% of the going rate, {rate} eb). Waits until {date}.
Staff.NoApplicants: No applicants waiting for this role.
Staff.LoyaltyHint: Loyalty rises with paid weeks, good months and bonuses, and falls with missed wages, extra shifts, cuts and refused raises. Sullen staff may quit, and steal; devoted staff try harder and ignore rivals' offers.
Staff.LoyaltyPc: A player character's loyalty is their own.
Staff.CannotManage: Only a partner who can act for the business can manage its staff.
Staff.Caught: Caught stealing: can be let go without severance.
Staff.Hurt: Hurt at work: off this week.
Staff.Asks: Asks for a raise to {pct}% of the going rate.
Staff.PayNow: Paid {wage} eb a week: {pct}% of the going rate ({rate} eb) for their skill in this role.
Staff.PayHint: A change of pay needs a majority. A raise lifts loyalty; a cut hurts it more than the difference.
Staff.AskText: They ask for {pct}% of the going rate ({wage} eb a week) by the month's end. Ignored, it counts as refused.
Staff.BonusHint: Paid now from the business's cash, once a week: each quarter of a week's wage lifts loyalty. A player character's goes to their eddies.

BonusQuarter.1: A quarter of a week's wage ({amount} eb)

Staff.MoveHint: Moves them at once, at the same share of the going rate for their skill in the new role.
Staff.FireHint: Needs a majority. They are paid a week's wage ({amount} eb) and anything owed. Letting a sullen employee go may bring trouble later.
Staff.FireCaught: Needs a majority. Caught stealing, they get no severance, only anything owed.
Staff.VetHint: Check every applicant for this role at once: Human Perception (an interview), Library Search (a records search) or Interface, DV {dv}, costing {cost} eb. A pass shows any hidden trait; a strong pass also their exact skill.
Staff.VetFailed: Vetted: the checks told you nothing.
Staff.ApplicantAsks: Asks {pct}% of the going rate for their skill. Waits until {date}.

Staff.OnCallHint: A player character on the staff can be asked for one of this week's rolls: a free action slot, the week's event, or a help. They roll it themselves, from their own Job view, with their own skills and Luck. It is one of their two overtime shifts, and the overtime is paid from the cash onto their payslip.

Staff.TeamLoyaltyHint: An Exec's team answer to their own Loyalty. Each week the save is 1d6 under it: one who fails neither takes a task nor does their job that week. A week with nothing done for them costs 1, and at 0 or below they betray you and go.
Staff.TeamRefuses: Refusing to work this week: see their Loyalty.
Staff.TeamCareHint: Each once a week. Loyalty can run past 10 until the week closes.

TeamCare.timeOff: A paid week off (+{gain}, no work this week)

Staff.TeamHint: An Exec can staff their Teamwork team as employees. Ranks 3, 5 and 9 each bring one member, so Teamwork {rank} gives you up to {size}. They take no wage (overtime is paid as if they were on the going rate), take a place on the staff like anyone, and leave if you leave the business. Their skill in the role follows your rank. They answer to their Loyalty: look after them on the Employee window. Replacing one you lost starts them at Loyalty 1, with 200 eb of hiring fees.
Staff.TeamLevel: A team member in this role would be {level} ({base}).
Staff.TeamDropHint: Or drag an NPC from the Actors directory here, for a team member you have already made: they keep their name and sheet, and their skill in the role follows your rank.
Staff.TeamPay: Unpaid: part of {name}'s team. Overtime is paid as if on the going rate.
Staff.GrantHint: The shareholders can grant an employee new shares, without a vote: up to {max}% of the company for all grants together, voted on by a majority of the shares. They vest after {weeks} weeks and are lost if the employee leaves first; once vested they are the employee's to keep, even if they leave. While they vest, loyalty rises by {loyalty} and stays at {floor} or above. A player character holds them in their own name and draws their share like any holder; an NPC holds them quietly, like an angel.
Staff.GrantVesting: {pct}% of the company in shares, vesting on {date}.
Staff.GrantVested: Holds {pct}% of the company in granted shares.

Staff.TrainHint: Once every {every} weeks, an NPC employee's best skill for their role can rise by 1: {perPoint} eb for each point of it now, from the business's cash. A partner whose own skill is higher can mentor them, spending {days} business days and rolling Education (or Persuasion, a step harder) at the business's DV: a failure teaches nothing, though the eb and days are spent. Otherwise it is a course, at twice the eb, which always teaches. Training adds at most {max} in all, and never takes a skill above {cap}. Their wage follows the new skill.
